[b]📌 Main Purpose[/b]

This is a sneak peek at one component of [b]Godly Hand[/b] — a full all-in-one NPC creator coming to Nexus. The Coordinate Picker solves a specific problem every NPC modder knows: finding tile coordinates for schedules and events without opening Tiled and counting by hand.

If you have ever made a custom NPC, you know the pain. You need a coordinate, so you open Tiled, squint at the grid, count tiles, write a number down, get it wrong by one, load the game, find out, and do it again. This tool replaces that entire process.

Load a map → click a tile → save the coordinate. That's it.

Works with all base game maps and any modded map that uses the standard .tbin or .tmx format.

[center]━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━[/center]

[b]⚙️ Features[/b]

⚠ Important — the tool cannot render a map without both the map file AND its tilesheet PNGs. It will tell you exactly which PNG files it needs so you know what to upload.

[b]🗺️ Loads tbin and tmx[/b]
Reads Stardew's native binary map format and Tiled's XML format. Handles base64+zlib compressed TMX layers — the default Tiled export format. If your map is tbin or tmx, it loads. Custom mods are supported as long as they use one of these two formats.

[b]✅ Tells you exactly which PNG tilesheets you need[/b]
After loading a map, a checklist shows every tilesheet it references. Each one is listed by filename — ticked green when loaded, shown in amber with the exact filename when still missing. You never have to guess which files to find.

[b]🖼️ Renders the full map with all layers[/b]
All layers are drawn in the correct order — Back, Buildings, Front, AlwaysFront — exactly as they appear in game. The map sits in a scrollable viewport. Switch between [b]0.5×, 1×, 2×, and 3× zoom[/b].

[b]📍 Click any tile to save its coordinates[/b]
Hover over the map to see a live X Y tooltip following your cursor. Click any tile to open a save prompt — type a label like "Nicholas morning position", choose a folder, and hit Save or press Enter. Saved tiles are highlighted green on the map so you can see at a glance what you have already recorded.

[b]📁 Organise into named folders[/b]
Create as many folders as you need — one per NPC, one per map, one per schedule block. Folders expand and collapse. Click a folder header to set it as the active save target so new coordinates go straight into it.

[b]📄 Export to .txt[/b]
When you are done, download a plain text file with all your folders and coordinates laid out cleanly, including the map name and X Y for every entry. Keep it open in Notepad while writing your schedule or event files.

[b]🧠 Tilesheet memory within a session[/b]
Once you upload a tilesheet PNG, it stays loaded for the rest of your session. If you switch to another map that shares tilesheets, those are already there — you only upload the new ones. This makes loading a second or third map much faster.

⚠ This memory does not survive closing the tab. If you close the tool and reopen it, you will need to upload all your tilesheet PNGs again from scratch. Keep your tilesheet folder somewhere easy to grabt. There's alot of maps in game. Organization is key.

[b]🚨 Nothing fails silently[/b]
If a file cannot be read, a popup tells you what went wrong. If a tilesheet fails to load, a warning appears. If something goes wrong during rendering, you get a message with the exact error. You will always know what happened and what to do next.

[b]📥 Installation[/b]

This tool runs entirely in your browser. There is nothing to install.

[b]HTML version — recommended for most users[/b]
[list]
[*]Download GodlyHand_CoordPicker.html[/*]
[*]Open it in Chrome, Firefox, or Edge[/*]
[*]Done — no setup required[/*]
[/list]
[b]JSX version — for Claude / React environments[/b]
[list]
[*]Download GodlyHand_CoordPicker.jsx[/*]
[*]Drop it into Claude.ai or any React sandbox and run it[/*]
[/list]
Both versions are identical in functionality. No internet connection required after downloading.

[b]📋 Requirements[/b]

[b]xnbcli by LeonBlade[/b]
Required to unpack Stardew Valley's .xnb files into .tbin format and extract tilesheet .png files. The tool cannot render a map without both. The [b]Guide tab[/b] inside the tool walks you through the full process step by step.
[url=https://github.com/LeonBlade/xnbcli]→ github.com/LeonBlade/xnbcli[/url]
Note that to get base game maps, you need to either get the game tbin files (What I use with this tool) or by some other method. The regular map file formate is not readable in current state.

[b]A modern browser[/b]
Chrome, Firefox, or Edge. No internet connection required after downloading the file.
